difficulty.from: question type (function of a paragraph); the RC bank has no difficulty field

answer.text: establish that a diffraction pattern must be interpreted rather than simply viewed
answer.line: Paragraph 4 says the pattern is not an image of the molecule. Turning it into a structure takes mathematics and judgment.

steps: Ask why the paragraph is there, not what it says. Function questions want the job.
Find the line the paragraph builds to: sentence 2. The pattern is a map of repeating distances, not a picture.
See where that pays off. In paragraph 6, Photo 51 speaks only "To anyone trained in the new diffraction theory of helices".

choices.text: argue that Astbury's photographs were more accurate than those taken later at King's
choices.note: Paragraph 5 says Wilkins and Gosling got sharper patterns than Astbury's. The passage ranks his pictures below the later ones.

choices.text: show that the technique was invented specifically to study the shape of DNA
choices.note: Sentence 1 describes the method for any fiber of long molecules. Nothing says it was invented for DNA.

choices.text: explain why Franklin preferred to study the A form rather than the B form
choices.note: Her reason for the A form, more exact numbers, is in paragraph 7. Paragraph 4 never mentions either form.

choices.text: establish that a diffraction pattern must be interpreted rather than simply viewed
choices.note: Sentence 2: a map of distances that takes mathematics and judgment to turn back into a structure.

choices.text: demonstrate that Astbury's fibers were too poorly ordered to reveal the structure
choices.note: Sentence 3 does say it, but one detail inside the paragraph is not the reason the author stops to explain how diffraction works.

spans.quote: The pattern is not an image of the molecule; it is a map of the distances that repeat inside it, and turning it back into a structure takes mathematics and judgment
spans.note: the job: a pattern has to be read, not just looked at

spans.quote: their fibers were too poorly ordered to say more
spans.choice: demonstrate that Astbury's fibers were too poorly ordered to reveal the structure
spans.note: a true detail, but not why the paragraph is there
